set.typical_award_size: Capitalized with $2,000,000 ARPA (ordinance Aug 2022), $1,700,000 ARPA added Dec 12, 2023, and a regular $200,000 annual General Fund contribution (formerly the Community Investment Fund). Awards through the November 2023 RFP/NOFA: $3,200,000 loan to The Hampstead Companies for Prospera at Homestead in Dixon (107 units at or below 60% AMI, 3% interest) and $93,000 to Napa-Solano Habitat for Humanity (three homes, Fairfield). Oct 2024: $1,500,000 for site work on the County-owned 580 North 1st Street, Dixon parcel (demolition approved Sept 22, 2026). Aug 4, 2026: Board approved a $400,000 loan (3% simple interest, payments deferred to year seven) to EAH Housing for Tabor Commons, Fairfield (66 units: 41 at 30% AMI including 16 IDD units, 10 at 60% and 15 at 70% AMI), conditioned on the City of Fairfield contribution, plus deferral of about $446,354 in County public facilities fees, and a $200,000 grant to Habitat for Harmony Village, Vacaville (10 ownership homes at or below 80% AMI). These awards fully committed the fund until the FY 2027-28 contribution.
set.affordability_requirement: Guidelines cap assisted households at 120% AMI (moderate income), with lower limits set by each RFP/NOFA; Prospera restricted to 60% AMI, Tabor Commons 30% to 70% AMI, Habitat homes 80% AMI, County workforce site 80% AMI. Loan payments recycle into the fund.
set.next_deadline: No open round as of November 9, 2026. The Aug 4, 2026 awards committed the full available balance and the FY 2026-27 contribution, leaving no uncommitted funds until the FY 2027-28 $200,000 contribution. The last RFP was November 2023; guidelines allow an RFP or NOFA at least once per funding cycle and let the Board allocate funds to a specific project at any time.
set.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 9, 2026: Legistar file 26-597 (Aug 4, 2026) shows the Tabor Commons loan and Habitat grant were approved and that the fund is fully committed until FY 2027-28; Tabor Commons unit mix is 30% to 70% AMI, not 20% to 50%. SCHTF guidelines allow up to 120% AMI. Prevailing wage true is uncited; remaining capital is General Fund money, not ARPA.

reason: Material: record showed the Aug 2026 awards as proposed with a 20 to 50 percent AMI mix and did not say the fund is fully committed until FY 2027-28; the Board approved them Aug 4, 2026 for a 30 to 70 percent AMI project and the Habitat grant funds homeownership.

set.typical_award_size: No adopted waiver or deferral program. The County has never waived public facilities fees but defers them case by case: MidPen Fair Haven Commons, Fairfield (2020, due at permanent loan closing or 30 months after building permit) and EAH Tabor Commons, Fairfield (approved Aug 4, 2026, about $446,354 deferred to first certificate of occupancy or five years after building permit, with rates frozen at permit, consistent with SB 937). In Jan 2024 The Hampstead Companies asked the Board to waive $672,829 for Prospera at Homestead; the Board instead funded a $3,200,000 Housing Trust Fund loan.
set.next_deadline: No program or deadline. Request a deferral from the Board, typically alongside a Housing Trust Fund request; SB 937 (effective Jan 1, 2025) generally lets qualifying residential projects pay impact fees at certificate of occupancy.
